reason: This entire case's initial evidence base originates from an external ChatGPT Deep Research investigation (2026-08-14 to 2026-08-16), not from this repository's own live collection process. Consistent with this investigation's established discipline for externally-sourced material (see DFAPTI-BB-2026-00001's RUN-0064 and RUN-0066), nothing in that corpus is treated as independently confirmed merely because a separate AI system located it. Every evidence item ingested from it is recorded at classification "Requires Verification" (or "Secondary Reference" for the corpus documents themselves) and verification_state "Unverified", regardless of how the source corpus itself labelled the underlying claim (e.g. its own "VERIFIED"/"FACT" markings). Upgrading any item to "Verified"/"Accepted" requires this investigation to independently fetch or otherwise confirm the underlying primary source itself.
impact: Every EV-0001 through EV-0036 item in this case's register carries verification_state "Unverified" as at case creation, regardless of source content. Future runs that independently confirm a specific item should add a new evidence entry (or update via the append-only correction pattern) rather than silently upgrading the existing record's verification_state.

reason: The external research corpus this case was ingested from contains approximately 230 numbered findings (F-001 to F-230, with a known gap where Snapshot 7 was never supplied) and a 763-question Continuing Investigation Question Bank, of which the corpus's own Answer Registers classify 519 as RESOLVED (15), PARTIAL (70), OPEN - PRIMARY RECORD (373), or OPEN - ANALYTICAL (61). Mechanically transcribing every one of these as an individual MAYHEM register entry in a single ingestion pass was judged not worth the transcription-error risk it would carry, and not necessary to make the case usable: this case's Evidence Register, Chronology, Contradiction Register and Open Question Register instead promote a curated set of the highest-value confirmed facts, negative-search findings, RESOLVED answer-register items, and messaging contradictions (36 evidence items, 19 chronology entries, 2 contradictions, 16 open questions). The complete corpus is preserved in full at cases/DFAPTI-MNC-2026-00001/preserved/ (EV-0034, EV-0035) specifically so later runs can promote further items from it without re-acquiring the source material.
impact: This case's registers are a first pass, not a complete atomisation of the source corpus. A future run continuing this case should treat the preserved corpus, not just the current register, as the full evidence base to draw further items from - most of the question bank's ~700 remaining items and most of the 230 findings have not yet been individually registered.

reason: This case is the first new case added to mayhem-investigations since DFAPTI-BB-2026-00001, and required resolving the open data-layer architecture question this repository's own README had deliberately left unanswered. Per DEC-0019 (in DFAPTI-BB-2026-00001's own decision register) and scripts/case-registry.js, this case's evidence data lives at cases/DFAPTI-MNC-2026-00001/data/ - a dedicated per-case directory - rather than at the repository root (which remains DFAPTI-BB-2026-00001's, grandfathered for backward compatibility) or in a separate repository (ruled out by the standing "mayhem investigations only" operating constraint).
impact: Establishes the pattern every future case will follow: cases/<CASE-ID>/data/, registered in scripts/case-registry.js, validated independently by scripts/validate.js.

reason: Per this investigation's live/frozen-snapshot gating model (established for DFAPTI-BB-2026-00001), only the DFAPTI (evidence) stage is built for this case at creation. DFAPTA, Lattice Atlas, the Temporal Projection Integrity Engine, the Enforcement Notice, and the Advocacy Package are not built and must not be built until the case operator issues an explicit "freeze evidence register" command for this case specifically - a freeze command for DFAPTI-BB-2026-00001 does not apply here, and vice versa. The case gate page presents the five downstream stages as locked/pending rather than omitting them, so the six-stage structure stays visible and consistent across cases.
impact: cases/DFAPTI-MNC-2026-00001/ currently contains only a dfapti/ workspace. No dfapta/, lattice-atlas/, temporal-projection-integrity-engine/, enforcement-notice/, or advocacy-package/ directory exists for this case yet.

reason: The case operator located and supplied Snapshot 7, filling the gap recorded at NOTE-0008. Verified by hash that it was not already present among the preserved files before processing it (avoiding the SRC-0106-style duplicate mistake this repository has previously made in DFAPTI-BB-2026-00001, see that case's DEC-0018). Applied the same curation discipline as RUN-0001 (DEC-0002): promoted the highest-value findings rather than transcribing all ten (F-131-F-140), and declined to register a contradiction for the 'assess first' vs 'prepare to scale' sequence because Snapshot 7 itself explicitly states these are not contradictory - manufacturing a contradiction the source document itself disclaims would be a worse error than under-registering one.
impact: The corpus gap noted in preserved/README.md and NOTE-0008 is closed. The case's Evidence Register grows from 36 to 42 items, Open Question Register from 16 to 18, Chronology from 19 to 20 entries.

reason: The case operator directly flagged that the Evidence Register (42 items) was too thin relative to the size of the source corpus (230 findings, 519 classified answer-register items). Re-examined DEC-0002's original curation call in light of that feedback and concluded it had erred too far toward compactness: a MAYHEM evidence register's job is to be the durable, browsable record of what the investigation has found, and leaving ~190 already-researched findings sitting only in unstructured preserved text files defeated that purpose even though the underlying research had already been done. Reversed course: parsed and ingested every numbered finding across all twelve snapshots (RUN-0003) rather than a curated subset. Where a finding's own snapshot supplied a specific external URL (only Snapshot 6 did this consistently, at the individual-finding level), that URL is cited directly and a new Source Register entry created if not already present. Where a snapshot only supplied an end-of-document source list not cleanly mappable to individual findings (every other snapshot), the evidence item cites its exact preserved file and finding number instead of inventing a specific external citation the source material didn't actually provide at that granularity - preserving honesty about precision over the appearance of completeness.
impact: Evidence Register grows from 42 to 262 items; Source Register from 43 to 72. The remaining under-mined layer is the two Answer Registers (519 RESOLVED/PARTIAL/OPEN-classified items across all 763 Question Bank entries) - not ingested in this run, and a candidate for a further expansion pass if the operator wants that depth too.

reason: Operator confirmed DEC-0006's flagged next step: ingest the two Answer Registers (519 classified Question Bank items) in addition to the 230 Deep Research Snapshot findings. Extended the same full-coverage, no-selective-curation approach used in RUN-0003 rather than treating RESOLVED/PARTIAL and OPEN items differently - an OPEN - PRIMARY RECORD answer ('no evaluation has been publicly located') is itself a recorded negative-search result with the same evidentiary status as this case's other negative findings (e.g. EV-0021, EV-0027, EV-0042), not a lesser category needing a different register.
impact: Evidence Register grows from 262 to 781 items - effectively the complete external research corpus (all findings and all classified question-bank answers) is now individually represented in the live, browsable register, not just described in preserved source files. This case's Evidence Register is now the largest in the repository, well exceeding DFAPTI-BB-2026-00001's 73 items - appropriate given the scale of the source material actually supplied, not a data-quality problem.
